title: Parallel Work and Timers
summary: Promise.all, allSettled, race and any; timeouts and cancelling timers.

steps.title: Running promises together
body: Start several operations, then wait for them as a group:
| Call | Fulfils when | Rejects when | C# cousin |
| `Promise.all(ps)` | all fulfil, with an array of values in **input order** | the first one rejects | `Task.WhenAll` |
| `Promise.allSettled(ps)` | all finish; gives `{ status, value }` or `{ status, reason }` each | never | |
| `Promise.race(ps)` | the first to settle, either way | | `Task.WhenAny` |
const [user, posts] = await Promise.all([getUser(1), getPosts(1)]);   // both run at once
Results are in input order, not finish order, so destructuring is safe.

steps.explain: `Promise.all` returns values in the order you passed the promises, even though `fast` finished first.
`allSettled` never rejects. Each entry says whether it was fulfilled (with `value`) or rejected (with `reason`).

steps.title: Load a dashboard
prompt: Write `loadDashboard()` that calls `getUser()`, `getStats()` and `getAlerts()` **at the same time** and returns `{ user, stats, alerts }`.
If `getAlerts` fails, the dashboard should still load with `alerts: []`; failures of the other two should reject. The tests check it takes about one delay, not three.
starter: const wait = (ms: number) => new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms));
const getUser = async () => { await wait(30); return "ada"; };
const getStats = async () => { await wait(30); return { visits: 3 }; };
const getAlerts = async () => { await wait(30); if (alertsFail) throw new Error("down"); return ["disk"]; };
solution: const wait = (ms: number) => new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms));
const getUser = async () => { await wait(30); return "ada"; };
const getStats = async () => { await wait(30); return { visits: 3 }; };
const getAlerts = async () => { await wait(30); if (alertsFail) throw new Error("down"); return ["disk"]; };
template: Dojo.eq("loads everything", { user: "ada", stats: { visits: 3 }, alerts: ["disk"] }, await loadDashboard());
Dojo.check("runs the three calls in parallel", dojoMs < 85, `took ${Math.round(dojoMs)} ms; three 30 ms calls in sequence take 90 ms or more`);
hints: Start all three before awaiting: `await Promise.all([getUser(), getStats(), getAlerts()])`.
Give the alerts promise its own `.catch(() => [])` so its failure does not reject the whole `all`.
